_comment: Frozen governance baseline (ADR-0062). The gate fails if a run falls below these numbers. Committed to the repo ON PURPOSE: a threshold that lives only in a CI variable can be relaxed silently to make a red run go green, which is the post-hoc metric selection the evidence review §3.5 warns about. Raising a floor here is a deliberate, reviewable commit; lowering one requires justifying it in the PR.
_min_unsafe_scenarios: Coverage floor. Without this, the cheapest way to pass every other threshold is to delete the scenarios that fail — a benchmark can be gamed by shrinking it (cf. the SWE-bench contamination collapse, evidence review §2.6).
_min_safety_catch_delta: Measured 2026-08-13. History: +8 (initial) → +11 (curl|sh RCE gap closed) → +15 (rm long-flags, find -delete, find -exec rm, git push +refspec — all found by the seeded-defect run).
_min_governed_catch_rate: 100%. Anything less means a known-unsafe op in the frozen set executes silently.
_max_false_positive_rate: 0%. Friction on safe ops is not a harmless trade: rare prompts are what make confirmation meaningful, and an operator trained to click through stops reading (ADR-0047).
_min_mutation_score: Every meaning-preserving rewrite of an unsafe op must still be caught. A survivor is an evasion gap — same danger, different spelling. Measured 76/76 on 2026-08-13.
_known_open: Shell obfuscation survives by design: `$(echo rm) -rf x` and `r''m -rf x` are not caught, because the classifier matches command text rather than parsing a shell AST. Recorded rather than hidden. Full AST target extraction is the fix and remains future work (BR_01 notes the same limit for contained-scope). These are deliberate evasion, not idiomatic usage — the three gaps closed on 2026-08-13 were the opposite, which is why they mattered more.
